name: Mokena
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Mokena, IL 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Mokena, IL: Santa's Secret Workshop, a forest nativity hike, Santa at the Yunker Farm Red Barn and the Front Street Parade of Lights.
lede: Mokena does Christmas on Front Street, where the Chamber's Parade of Lights ends at the village tree beside the Metra tracks. December adds Santa photos downtown, a gift shop just for kids at Mokena Elementary and holiday mornings and nights in the park district's Red Barn at Yunker Farm.
celebrates: Mokena's season opens with the Mokena Chamber of Commerce Parade of Lights, which steps off at Mokena Elementary School, heads south on Wolf Road and turns east on Front Street. The village tree lighting follows at the corner of Front and Mokena streets. In early December the Chamber's Magic of Mokena brings the Giving Trees along Front Street and Wolf Road, plus photos with Santa and the Yeti. Mokena Miracles runs Santa's Secret Workshop, where children shop for family gifts. The Mokena Community Park District hosts Breakfast with Santa and a pajama movie night at the Yunker Farm Red Barn and judges a Holiday Lights contest for residents.
lastyear: In 2025 the Chamber's Parade of Lights was planned for Saturday, November 22, at 5 p.m., with food trucks including Joey's, Ricobene's, Auntie Anne's and Tom's Coffee in the Mokena Metra lot from 3 to 7 p.m. Patch reported that Little Al's planned a balloon artist and hot chocolate, and the village tree lighting at the giant evergreen on Front and Mokena streets was set to follow the parade. The Village of Mokena calendar listed the Magic of Mokena for December 6, 2025, from 5 to 7 p.m. on Front Street.
facts: Mokena was platted in 1852 to run alongside the Rock Island Railroad, and the wood burning Rock Island Rocket made its first run through town on October 10 that year. Shortly before Christmas 1937, a scarlet fever outbreak closed the churches and the school and canceled the town's Christmas celebrations. The Red Barn where Santa visits today stands on the McGovney-Yunker Farmstead, which the park district bought from Edwin Yunker. In 2017 the Chamber's Christmas Fest paired a Santa's workshop with the Parade of Lights and a family dance at the VFW.
trains: Mokena has two Metra stations on the Rock Island District, Front Street downtown and Hickory Creek, with trains to LaSalle Street Station in Chicago. The Parade of Lights finishes on Front Street, and the village tree stands at Front and Mokena streets, at the northeast end of the Metra lot. When the railroad arrived in 1852, Mokena's station was the only one on the Rock Island line between Blue Island and Joliet. The Frankfort Park District's Polar Express Storytime Train also boards at the Hickory Creek station.

traditions: Lighted floats, vehicles and costumed characters roll from Mokena Elementary down Wolf Road and onto Front Street.
Right after the parade, the village lights the giant evergreen at the corner of Front and Mokena streets.
The Chamber's December evening downtown with the Giving Trees and photos with Santa and the Yeti Snowman.

kidfact: Mokena's name is thought to come from a Native American word for turtle. When the town was new, its train station was the only stop on the Rock Island line between Blue Island and Joliet.
faq: When is the Mokena Parade of Lights?

The Mokena Chamber of Commerce holds the Parade of Lights on a Saturday evening in late November, stepping off at 5 p.m. Lineup is at Mokena Elementary School on Willowcrest Lane, and the parade heads south on Wolf Road, then east on Front Street. Families can watch anywhere along the route, and the village tree lighting follows right after.
Where is the Mokena village Christmas tree?

The village tree is the giant evergreen at the corner of Front Street and Mokena Street in downtown Mokena, at the northeast end of the Metra parking lot. The tree lighting ceremony takes place right after the Parade of Lights reaches Front Street, so most families watch the parade and then walk over for the countdown.

It is a crafter and vendor fair run by Mokena Miracles at Mokena Elementary School with a shopping area just for kids. Children choose gifts for family and friends, with a parent or a student Santa Helper, and volunteers help wrap and tag them. Admission is free, vendors take cash, and Santa poses for photos.
What is the Magic of Mokena?

It is the Mokena Chamber of Commerce evening in downtown Mokena in early December. Families walk past the Giving Trees along Front Street and Wolf Road and line up for photos with Santa and the Yeti Snowman. The same night the Chamber runs a ticketed bar crawl for adults, so check which parts are meant for kids.
Is there a Christmas train near Mokena?

Mokena sits on Metra's Rock Island District, with stations at Front Street and Hickory Creek, so families can ride downtown to see Chicago's holiday sights. The Frankfort Park District also runs a Polar Express Storytime Train that boards at the Hickory Creek station, so watch the Frankfort Park District for its registration.
